title: High-order Simulation of Nearly Hydrostatic Atmospheric Flows
summary: Accurate simulation of atmospheric flows is challenging. Low-Mach-number dynamics often need to be resolved in the presence of a dominant, nearly hydrostatic background state. Conventional upwind numerical fluxes can introduce excessive acoustic-speed-based dissipation in the low-Mach regime. Discretization errors in the balance law can also generate spurious motion. This work investigates these two issues within a high-order Direct Flux Reconstruction (DFR) framework coupled with a third-order exponential time integrator for the 3D compressible Euler equations with gravity.
